root_cause_label: No stair-building logic; gold unreachable without elevation strategy; also misidentified win condition as 'pickup' on gold cell
one_sentence_failure_summary: From the very first implementation the agent never understood that winning requires moving onto the gold cell (not calling 'pickup') or that reaching elevation 8 requires systematically collecting blocks and dropping them to build a staircase, so every revision wanders without ever achieving the goal.
t_err_evidence: agent writes solution.js with faulty logic: 'pickup' on gold, no stair-building strategy
t_commit_evidence: Step 4 establishes the two fundamental flaws (wrong win action, no stair-building plan) that persist unchanged through all subsequent revisions (steps 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21). Every rewrite either drops all drop logic (step 16, 21) or retains the same wrong 'pickup' on gold, locking in failure from the first implementation.
t_surface_evidence: test runner produces only 'DEBUG: invoking game.run(3)' with no win output, trials never complete
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge about two key game mechanics: (1) the win condition is triggered by moving the player onto the gold cell (the z() movement function sets s=true when entering a type===3 cell), not by issuing 'pickup' on it; (2) reaching the gold at elevation 8 requires building a staircase by collecting blocks and dropping them in sequence, since the player can only traverse cells within ±1 elevation difference. Without understanding these mechanics the agent's code could never succeed.
